standard_prerequisites.name: The top cohomology of a product is one dimensional
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (B) identifying the cohomology of a product with the tensor product, and the axiom making the top cohomology of an equidimensional variety one dimensional
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the target of the degree map of the product is one dimensional and generated by the class of a product of closed points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The degree of the class of a closed point is one
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the classical version of the commutativity of the degree map with the degree of zero cycles
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes the degree of the class of a product point as one.

standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplicativity of the cycle class map for exterior products
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axioms (C)(a) and (C)(c) on compatibility with pullbacks and with exterior products
standard_prerequisites.use: Expresses the class of a product point as the exterior product of the classes of the factors.

core_obligations: Identify the top cohomology (proof lines 1722-1730): by the product axiom the top cohomology of the product is the tensor product of the top cohomologies of the factors, which is one dimensional by the axiom on the top cohomology of an equidimensional variety.

Compare on a generator (proof lines 1730-1737): the classical degree computation shows that this one dimensional space is generated by the class of a product of closed points and that the degree of that class is one; the class of a product of points is the exterior product of the classes of the points, whose degrees are one, so the tensor product of the two degree maps agrees with the degree map of the product on a generator and hence everywhere.
proof_roadmap: Use the product axiom and one dimensionality of the top cohomology.
Verify the identity on the class of a product of closed points.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a classical Weil cohomology theory the degree map of a product of smooth projective varieties is the tensor product of the degree maps of the factors (statement lines 1718-1722). The proof (proof lines 1723-1737) identifies the one dimensional top cohomology of the product and compares the two maps on the class of a product of closed points. H2: a complete short computation.
